steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers → Local engine card
steps.path: Round 2 of P-1: the card, re-laid
steps.headline: The engine card is a title with its state, one fact line, and two rows: a faster engine when your chip has one, and Advanced.
steps.changed: Round 1 had a state line, a hardware line, a 'Using:' line with a button, and a bare '› Advanced'. Now: 'Local engine · Running', then one line — chip · GB loaded · last reply read/write speed — then a 'Faster engine for your AMD chip' row with a Set up / Switch button, then an 'Advanced' row with the same right-hand chevron every settings row has. Version and backend moved into Advanced.
steps.notice: Less to read, and the two things you might act on are rows you already know how to use. The button for a faster engine only appears when the app has found the matching chip.
steps.risk: Nothing on this card tells you the engine version any more until you open Advanced.

steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers → Local engine card
steps.path: Round 2 of P-2 and P-3: setting up ROCm, and no more 'refused' state
steps.headline: Set up shows one sentence, the command with Copy inside it, and two buttons; the switch is only offered when it will work.
steps.changed: The box under the faster-engine row: 'Install AMD's ROCm software first' (with an (i)), 'Run this in a terminal (Arch Linux). It will ask for your password.', the command with Copy beside it, then Run in terminal and Check again. The four-button row and the extra paragraph are gone. The app now checks for the chip AND its software before offering the button at all, so the round-1 'refused' screen is no longer a normal state — a failure after install still shows the engine's own message as an ordinary error line.
steps.notice: Two clicks and a password in your own terminal, nothing installed behind your back, and no button that leads to a refusal.
steps.risk: On a Linux flavour we cannot recognise, the box offers AMD's guide and Check again instead of a command.

steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers → Local engine card → Advanced
steps.path: Round 2 of P-4: shorter words, proper rows
steps.headline: Advanced opens in place: two speed switches with one-line hints, the context length, and the engine build and folder, all as rows.
steps.changed: 'Speculative decoding — Faster replies when text repeats.' and 'Compress context memory — Halves the memory long chats use.' Each keeps its (i) for the full story. Context length is a row with the number field on the right; the version, backend and models folder are one read-only row.
steps.notice: A student sees four short rows, not paragraphs; a power user still gets every fact and switch.
steps.risk: Changing either switch restarts the engine; a model in use reloads on the next message.

steps.path: Round 2 of P-5: one number, breakdown on hover
steps.headline: A model's size is one dotted number; hovering it breaks down model, vision file, download total and memory while running.
steps.changed: '3.3 GB · UD-Q4_K_XL · Runs fast — fits on your GPU'. The 3.3 GB carries a dotted underline; hover or tap opens a small table: Model file 2.4 GB · Vision file 0.9 GB · Download 3.3 GB · Memory while running 4.9 GB (includes 1.6 GB for a 32k context). The picture shows the bubble open on the first card.
steps.notice: The row is a single line again. The context-memory number is one hover away when 'tight' needs explaining.
steps.risk: The Before side has no recommended cards because master's workbench fixture had none; the real app shows the same cards with '2.4 GB · UD-Q4_K_XL'.

steps.path: Round 2 of P-6: icons, not a tag
steps.headline: An eye marks a model that sees images, a page marks text-only; hover names it. 'Add vision' is a short link.
steps.changed: The 'Sees images' tag is replaced by a small eye icon; text-only models get a page icon. Hovering either says 'Sees images' or 'Text only' (and, for a model that could see, points to the Add vision link). The Add vision line is just 'Add vision (0.9 GB)'.
steps.notice: You can tell at a glance which downloaded models take pictures, without an extra word on every row.
steps.risk: Icons need the hover bubble for their meaning; on a phone the bubble opens on tap.

steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers → Models → a model's Settings
steps.path: Round 2 of P-7: the settings panel as rows
steps.headline: A model's settings are ordinary Settings rows: Context length, Keep loaded, and an Advanced row for GPU layers and flags.
steps.changed: Every setting is a row with a title, a one-line hint and its control on the right. 'Context length — Blank uses the engine's setting.' 'Keep loaded — Never put this model to sleep.' 'Advanced' expands in place with the right-hand chevron turned down: 'Layers on graphics chip' (Auto or a number) and 'Extra engine flags' (a text box), both with an (i).
steps.notice: It reads like the rest of Settings. A first-time user sees two plain rows; a power user opens Advanced.
steps.risk: Extra flags are unchecked by design: a wrong one stops that model from loading until it is fixed, with the engine's message shown here.

steps.surface: New session form → model picked → memory warning
steps.path: Round 2 of P-8: one line, details on request
steps.headline: The memory warning is one line with a Why? that unfolds the numbers and the don't-warn-again box.
steps.changed: The app's thin status strip (amber dot, one sentence, one action) replaces the boxed warning. Why? unfolds '9.5 GB model + 15.6 GB for 128k context…', the explanation, and 'Don't warn me again for this model at this context length'. 'Too large' uses the same strip with no checkbox: it is not a choice. The picture shows it unfolded.
steps.notice: The form stays short; the warning reads in a glance and explains itself only when asked.
steps.risk: The remembered answer lives on this computer only.
